findings.title: Removing `findMany` breaks existing consumers
findings.body: This PR deletes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, but the diff updates no call sites. `InsightsBookingService` is exported and was previously responsible for executing the denormalized query; any consumer still calling `findMany` will fail TypeScript compilation or runtime. Either migrate every call site in this PR or keep a `findMany` wrapper that executes a raw query using `getBaseConditions()`.

findings.title: Unparenthesized OR authorization condition can be miscombined by callers
findings.body: When scope is `team` or `org` and no filter conditions are supplied, `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly. For those scopes `authConditions` is a top-level `OR` such as `(team booking) OR (user booking)`. If a caller appends another predicate, e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "startTime" >= ...`, SQL precedence makes it `(team booking) OR ((user booking) AND date filter)`, so the extra predicate is applied only to one branch. The returned fragment should always be wrapped in parentheses, otherwise date/security predicates can be silently skipped for part of the dataset.

findings.title: Composite `Prisma.Sql` expectations are not structurally equal to reduce-built fragments
findings.body: The service builds org/team and combined-filter conditions through `reduce` using nested fragments like `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR (${condition})` and `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) AND (${condition})`. The expectations at lines 295, 332, and 429 are single flat `Prisma.sql` templates. `Prisma.Sql` equality is structural over its internal `strings` and `values`, not based on the rendered SQL text, so a nested fragment built with `reduce` will not deep-equal a flat template even when the SQL renders identically. These assertions will fail; compare rendered SQL or execute the query instead of using `toEqual` on `Prisma.Sql` objects.

findings.title: Exact SQL array order depends on unordered repository results
findings.body: The expected SQL hard-codes the order of `teamIds` and user IDs inside `ANY([...])`. `teamIds` comes from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and user IDs come from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`; neither call specifies an `orderBy`. If Postgres returns those rows in a different order, the `ANY` arrays differ even though the authorization semantics are identical, and the exact `Prisma.sql` comparison fails intermittently. Sort the IDs before asserting or compare semantically.

findings.title: No database execution coverage for org/team `ANY` conditions
findings.body: The only test that actually executes the generated conditions against Postgres uses `scope: "user"`. The org/team authorization paths, which are the only places that emit `ANY(${array})`, are only compared as `Prisma.sql` strings and never run against the database. A real parameter-binding/type-inference problem in those paths (for example around array parameters) would therefore pass the test suite while failing in production. Add a `$queryRaw` execution test for at least one org/team scope.
